Keywords: Heavy Arbalest and Arming Sword Routiers
RagShortTexts: Routier companies offer rulers sustained armed service for payment.
The same company may support a garrison while threatening nearby food-producing households.

Variants.Content: The Brabançons and routiers were mercenary infantry companies recruited from the Low Countries. They fought as cohesive free companies armed with heavy crossbows, bills, and arming swords, and they campaigned throughout the year for any employer who paid in silver. Their service carried no regard for papal bans, since the Third Lateran Council had condemned them and their bands kept fighting anyway. Their discipline made them useful in sieges and in pacification campaigns, but their habit of living off the countryside bred hatred among the peasantry. Rulers valued them because they could be hired at short notice, and they valued them less once the wars ended.

Monarchs preferred routiers to the unruly feudal levies that could serve only forty days. Their endurance made them indispensable for long castle blockades and pacification campaigns across Aquitaine and Normandy. A lord who hired a routier band had to pay its wages on schedule, or the company would turn its arms against his own lands. Contracts were sealed, and each captain kept the originals.

Villagers dread the approach of Brabancon baggage trains. They pillage cellars down to dry barley meal and hang resisters, yet their unyielding battle discipline earns dread on field lines. Wanderers who stumble on their camps learn quickly to keep silent and hide what food they carry.
